text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Central planning bureau is forecasting record job growth
of 134,000 for next year. (p1)
- Amsterdam's AEX index suffers biggest daily drop since
- KLM rejects European Commission's position on
discount fares on the Amsterdam-London route. (p3)
- Philips Electronics and Japan's Sony
and Hewlett Packard launch their own standard for
DVD-Ram. (p3)
- Window coverings maker Hunter Douglas reports
1997 first- half net up by 21.3 pct at Dfl 76.3 mln. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Businesses foresee fiscal conflicts over proposed tax
reform of company share option schemes. (p1)
- Life insurers neglect their obligation to provide
information, says insurer ombudsman. (p2)
- Nedelev divests of all its shares in port services company
Hes Beheer. (p13)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Number of pigs in the Netherlands rose by 700,000 in spite
of massive destruction of pigs to fight swine fever. (p1)
- Net profit and turnover of Aalberts Industries
rises to Dfl 16.4 mln and Dfl 300 mln respectively in first six
months. (p29)
- U.S. electric appliances giant General Electric to
start the sale of light bulbs in the Netherlands. (p29)
TROUW
- KLM denies the use of dirty tricks to force EasyJet from
the market. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Food and detergent giant Unilever
creates confusion around its ice-cream brand Soledo. (p9)
